<!--
One claim per issue. The claim-card format is in claims/README.md:
https://github.com/Freedom-Jack/briefbench/blob/main/claims/README.md
A link and a short paraphrase in your own words are enough. Don't paste whole articles or long quotes.
Only advice about prompts (what a prompt says or how it says it) or about settings (which model, effort level or
multi-agent mode to run a task with). Other advice about the agent's setup, such as tools, project files like
CLAUDE.md, checks outside the model or how several agents are arranged, is out of scope.
Issues are public: no private prompts, outputs or keys.
Recording a claim doesn't mean it works. It changes the skill only if a test supports it.
-->

## Source

<!-- Link, author, and the publication date or the date you read it. -->

## The claim

<!-- One assertion, in your own words. Keep your interpretation for the sections below. -->

## Conditions

<!-- The kind of work, such as coding, and the models or hosts the source says it applies to. "Not stated" is fine. -->

## Connection to brief

<!-- Your interpretation: what it might change in the skill, and why. The skill improves a prompt and may add a note suggesting settings; it doesn't choose methods, change settings or do the task. -->

## Known evidence

<!-- Supporting or contrary evidence you know of, with links. "None known" is fine. -->

## Possible test
